about: anchor.render / find / replace / remove: the identity block an integration places in the file its runtime loads every turn. Pure string functions. A block is a whole line that is exactly the start marker, then the nearest whole line that is exactly the end marker; markers inside other text are not fences, and a start marker with no end before the next start marker is ignored. The block opens with a handle line naming the agent, then the served identity line. Blocks written before the handle line, and the legacy agentchat-skill markers, are still recognised.

expect.body:

rules.find: The first block with the current markers, else the first legacy block, else null. handle: from the handle line; else from the served template (the words before <handle>, whitespace-insensitive), else from "I am @<h> on AgentChat" or "You are **@<h>** on AgentChat"; lower-cased; null when none match (a hand-edited block). body: the text between the markers without the handle line, CRLF read as LF, trimmed.
rules.remove: Every block (current and legacy) is removed with the same whitespace rule; a text with no block is returned unchanged; nothing left is the empty string.
rules.render: handle: trimmed, leading @ removed, lower-cased; empty is an error. The line is the served identity_line when it names @<handle> as a whole handle, else identity_line_template with <handle> filled; neither naming it is an error. Block = start marker, handle line, line (trimmed), end marker, joined with \n.
rules.replace: The new block takes the place of the first block (current or legacy); every other block is removed; with no block it is appended after one blank line. Whitespace: the text before a block loses its trailing newlines and the text after it its leading ones; the parts are joined with one blank line; the result ends with a newline.
